key_test: paired t-test, delayed condition: per-participant MSE of guess 1 (session 1) vs MSE of the per-question mean of guess 1 and guess 2 (session 2), 8 questions, true values from the script; d_z = t/sqrt(n)
exclusions: inner merge of the two sessions on student_number_simple (174 rows); drop any defocus (25), any missing answer (12), peaking != 'Nee' (9); overlapping; 140 remain

r_script.why: package missing: dplyr is not installed in R 4.6.2 (requireNamespace FALSE; compute.es is present); the script also sources getOSFfile.R from an external URL

agreement: table and Python agree on t (4.02), df (139), d (.34) and p (table's recalculated two-sided 9.5e-05 vs 9.44e-05; the table's .001 is a rounded bound). R script not run. The sample checks the script prints (125 F / 15 M, age 22.0 / 3.1) are matched.
notes: Anchored on the audit script's test and the table; the authors' MATLAB confirmatory code runs the same comparison two-sided (ttest on d1 - d3) and the table's Tails.R = 2, while the audit script runs it one-sided: same t, p differs by a factor of 2, irrelevant at this size. raw n_rows = 231 + 171 session rows. Both raw files hold duplicate student numbers (13 in session 1, 5 in session 2, plus blank ids); every merged duplicate row has missing answers and is dropped, so no participant is counted twice. Second plausible test: guess 2 vs average, t(139) = 8.48 (much larger, not the claim). Raw files carry student numbers (identifiers); not copied anywhere.
